user_requirement: Freeze the previously usable standard; after every public-dataset candidate, also retest the original device data and speed.
required_accounting: Every original query, including all known difficult and previously incorrect images; no outcome-driven deletion, label change or enrollment replacement.
Correct, wrong identity accepted, rejection and processing failure separately, overall and for every case.
Per-query transitions: correct-to-correct, correct-to-wrong, correct-to-rejected, wrong-to-correct, wrong-to-rejected, remaining wrong.
Counts correct within 2.0 and 2.5 seconds; P50, P95, maximum and first/warm query timing, with model/gallery ready and enrollment costs separate.
Original bytes and source template integrity; isolated payment databases, simulated transaction/cancellation guards and no production data overwrite.
Preserve all observations and exact candidate/model/configuration hashes, including failed candidates.
promotion_gates: All 168 outcomes complete; no previously correct identity becomes wrong, rejected or a processing failure.
Do not call wrong-to-rejected a genuine identification correction or count retry as correct.
An accuracy-improvement claim requires at least one genuine wrong-to-correct transition and no losses of previously correct cases.
A safety/rejection-only candidate must be labeled as such, with any correct-coverage loss explicit; it cannot be advertised as improved recognition accuracy or reduced matching work.

A speed-improvement claim needs same-host standard/candidate timing with matching runtime, gallery, thread/power conditions and complete accuracy accounting. Ambiguous timing warrants a bounded paired repeat, not repeat-until-pass selection.
First compare standard and candidate on Windows; do not assume historical Pi scores/times are bit-identical to Windows OpenCV reference registration.
Repeat original-data regression and timing on the reconnected Pi before claiming device improvement or promoting a candidate.
Leave standard branch/tag unchanged; promotion requires explicit user authorization even after regression passes.
scope_note: No new candidate is adopted by this protocol. The current full SMPD baseline remains frozen. Its missing-finger-valley examples are not required repair targets, but this does not authorize removing original-device regression queries.
